title: Enforcement Decree of the Korea International Cooperation Agency Act
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE KOREA INTERNATIONAL COOPERATION AGENCY ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Korea International Cooperation Agency Act and matters necessary for its enforcement. <Amended Apr. 16, 2019>

Article 2 (Procedures for Recommending Candidates for Standing Directors)
① A Standing Director Recommendation Committee shall be established in the Korea International Cooperation Agency (hereinafter referred to as the "Agency") to recommend candidates for standing directors under Article 8(3) of the Korea International Cooperation Agency Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act").
② The Standing Director Recommendation Committee under paragraph ① (hereinafter referred to as the "Recommendation Committee") shall consist of:
1. The Director-General of the Development Cooperation Bureau of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs;
2. Two standing directors elected by the board of directors under Article 12 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "board of directors");
3. Three external members elected by the board of directors from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience relating to the Agency's projects;
4. One employee recommended by an organization representing the employees of the Agency.
③ The chairperson of the Recommendation Committee shall be elected from among its members under paragraph ②.
④ Meetings of the Recommendation Committee shall open with a majority of all incumbent members present and adopt resolutions with the affirmative votes of a majority of those present.
⑤ The Recommendation Committee shall recommend as standing directors persons with extensive knowledge, experience, and capabilities necessary to perform the duties.
⑥ Matters necessary for the operation of the Recommendation Committee, including screening and recommendation of candidates and exclusion, challenge, or voluntary withdrawal of members, other than those specified in paragraphs ① through ⑤, shall be prescribed by the Agency's internal regulations.

Article 3 (Dispatch of Public Officials)
① Where the Agency requests the dispatch of public officials from a State agency under Article 14 of the Act, it shall specify the positions and duties to be assigned to the officials and their areas of expertise and qualifications, and submit the request through the Minister of Foreign Affairs. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013>
② The head of an agency receiving a request under paragraph ① may dispatch public officials affiliated with that agency to the Agency after consulting with the Minister of Foreign Affairs and obtaining approval from the Prime Minister. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013>
③ The number of dispatched public officials shall not exceed 30: Provided, That where there are grounds for dispatching more than 30 officials, the Minister of Foreign Affairs shall determine the number in consultation with the Minister of the Interior and Safety upon request by the Agency. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Feb. 29, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Nov. 19, 2014; July 26, 2017>
④ The Agency may pay allowances connected with assigned duties to dispatched public officials as prescribed by its articles of incorporation.

Article 4 (Dispatch of Experts Who Are Public Officials)
① Where experts or members of the Korean Youth Overseas Volunteer Corps dispatched to developing countries to carry out projects under Article 7 of the Act are public officials, such dispatch shall be deemed dispatch service under Article 32-4 of the State Public Officials Act or Article 30-4 of the Local Public Officials Act. Where the dispatch period is at least one year, Article 42 of the Decree on the Appointment of Public Officials or Article 27-3 of the Decree on the Appointment of Local Public Officials shall apply mutatis mutandis. <Amended Mar. 23, 1996; Jan. 29, 1999>
② Where a relevant foreign institution bears the living expenses of a dispatched expert who is a public official and the amount it pays is less than the living expenses paid by the Agency to other dispatched experts, the Agency may pay the difference within the limits of its budget.

Article 5 (Dispatch of Employees)
① Where the Agency deems it necessary to promote international cooperation, it may dispatch its employees to administrative agencies at various levels, government-invested institutions, other public organizations, etc.
② Where the Agency deems it necessary to promote international cooperation, it may dispatch its employees to international cooperation institutions or international organizations abroad with approval from the Minister of Foreign Affairs. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 6 (Contributions by Persons Other Than the Government)
For contributions by persons other than the Government under Article 15 of the Act, the method, procedures, and other relevant matters shall be determined by agreement between the contributor and the Agency.

Article 7 (Government Contributions)
① Where the Government intends to provide contributions to the Agency under Article 16(1) of the Act, the Minister of Foreign Affairs shall include them in the budget and provide them to the Agency. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013>
② By April 30 of each year, the Agency shall submit to the Minister of Foreign Affairs a budget request for contributions for the following year accompanied by:
1. A business plan and a plan for receipts and disbursements of funds for the following year;
2. An estimated statement of financial position and an estimated statement of profit or loss for the following year;
3. Other documents necessary to clarify the contents of the request for contributions. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013; Jan. 5, 2021>
③ When the budget for contributions under paragraph ① is finalized, the Minister of Foreign Affairs shall notify the Agency thereof. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 8 (Disbursement of Government Contributions)
① Where the Agency intends to receive government contributions, it shall submit to the Minister of Foreign Affairs an application for disbursement of contributions accompanied by a quarterly business plan and a quarterly budget execution plan at least 15 days before the beginning of the relevant quarter. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013>
② Where the Minister of Foreign Affairs finds the contents of an application under paragraph ① appropriate, the Minister shall disburse the contributions accordingly. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 9 (Loans and Free Use of State Property)
Where State property is lent free of charge to the Agency or its free use and enjoyment is permitted under Article 17 of the Act, the details, conditions, procedures, and other relevant matters shall be prescribed by a contract between the agency managing the relevant State property and the Agency.

Article 10 (Applications for Approval to Borrow Funds)
Where the Agency intends to obtain approval to borrow funds under Article 18 of the Act, it shall submit to the Minister of Foreign Affairs an application for approval stating:
1. Purpose of the borrowing;
2. Amount to be borrowed;
3. Lender;
4. Terms of borrowing;
5. Method and deadline for repayment;
6. Other matters necessary for borrowing and repaying the funds. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 10-2 Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2016>

Article 10-3 Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2016>

Article 10-4 Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2016>

Article 10-5 Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2016>

Article 10-6 Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2016>

Article 10-7 Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2016>

Article 11 (Approval of Business Plans and Budget Estimates)
① The Agency shall prepare a business plan and budget estimates for the following year and submit them to the Minister of Foreign Affairs by December 31 of each year for approval. The same shall apply to any amendment thereto. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013>
② Where necessary for preparing the business plan and budget estimates under paragraph ①, the Agency may request the heads of central administrative agencies to send relevant data and opinions through the Minister of Foreign Affairs. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 12 Deleted. <Apr. 16, 2019>

Article 13 (Disposal of Surplus)
Where a surplus arises upon settlement of accounts at the end of a business year, the Agency shall use the surplus to cover losses carried forward and carry the remainder forward to the following year.

Article 13-2 (Implementation of Projects through Public Competition)
① Where the Agency intends to publicly invite proposals from the public and private sectors for an individual project under Article 22-2(1) of the Act, it shall announce:
1. The schedule for public competition;
2. Eligibility for participation;
3. Estimated total project expenses and expenses for the relevant year;
4. Timing for implementing the project;
5. Standards and methods for project selection;
6. Other matters deemed necessary for implementing the individual project.
② In evaluating proposals invited under the latter part of Article 22-2(1) of the Act, the Agency shall comprehensively consider the capabilities, project performance record, project implementation plan, and creditworthiness of each person submitting a proposal.
③ The Agency shall establish and operate an evaluation committee to evaluate the proposals under the latter part of Article 22-2(1) of the Act.
④ Details of the evaluation standards under paragraph ② and the composition and operation of the evaluation committee under paragraph ③ shall be prescribed by the Agency's internal regulations.

Article 13-3 (Implementation of Projects under Agreements)
① Where the Agency intends to conclude an agreement with a foreign government, organization, or international organization under Article 22-2(2) of the Act, it shall consult with the other party in advance and finalize an implementation plan for the project covered by the agreement.
② Where the Agency deems it necessary for the effective implementation of projects under Article 7 of the Act, it may, before finalizing an implementation plan under paragraph ①, receive proposals from the other party to an agreement under Article 22-2(2) of the Act and review their feasibility.
③ Details of evaluation of the feasibility of proposals under paragraph ② and related matters shall be prescribed by the Agency's internal regulations.

Article 13-4 (Special Cases concerning Contracts)
① Where the Agency carries out a project overseas and deems it necessary in view of the purpose, scale, etc. of the project, it may conduct a tender in the country where the project is implemented, pursuant to the proviso to Article 22-2(4) of the Act.
② Where the Agency carries out a project overseas and deems it necessary in view of its purpose, scale, etc., it may, pursuant to the proviso to Article 22-2(4) of the Act, restrict the qualifications of tender participants to persons meeting all of the following requirements:
1. A person falling under either of the following items:
(a) Where a tender is held in the country where the project is implemented under paragraph ①, a corporation established under the laws of that country;
(b) A person meeting the standards prescribed by the Agency, taking into account statutes, institutions, practices, and other matters related to foreign cooperation projects in the country where the project is implemented;
2. A person meeting all of the following requirements:
(a) The person must not have been restricted from bidding, publicly declared ineligible for contracting, or otherwise sanctioned for such ineligibility by an international organization or foreign government;
(b) The person must not be under a restriction on eligibility to participate in bidding as an improper business operator under Article 27 of the Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party, Article 31 of the Act on Contracts to Which a Local Government Is a Party, or Article 39 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
(c) The person must not have been convicted of a bribery-related offense under domestic or foreign statutes.
③ Under the proviso to Article 22(4) of the Act, the Agency may prescribe contract terms differently with respect to any of the following:
1. Methods and standards for determining estimated prices under Articles 8 and 9 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party;
2. Overseas construction contracts under Article 48-2 of that Decree;
3. Contract performance guarantees under Article 50 of that Decree;
4. Inspection periods and methods under Article 55 of that Decree;
5. Payment of consideration under Article 58 of that Decree;
6. Adjustment of contract amounts due to price fluctuations under Article 64 of that Decree;
7. Other matters concerning the conclusion and performance of contracts under Chapter V of that Decree which the Minister of Foreign Affairs recognizes and publicly notifies as requiring different terms in view of statutes of the country where the project is implemented, international practice, etc.

Article 14 (Subsidiary Institutions)
Under Article 25 of the Act, the Agency may establish training institutes, research institutes, project units for incidental projects under Article 7, subparagraph 11 of the Act, and other necessary subsidiary institutions. <Amended June 30, 2001; Apr. 16, 2019>

Article 15 (Notification of Guidelines for Project Implementation)
The Minister of Foreign Affairs may establish and notify the Agency of guidelines necessary for its implementation of projects under Article 7 of the Act. <Amended Jan. 29, 1999; Mar. 23, 2013; Jan. 5, 2021>

Article 16 Deleted. <June 13, 2017>

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 13328, Mar. 18, 1991>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That Articles 2 and 3 of these Addenda shall enter into force on the date of completion of registration of the incorporation of the Agency.

Article 2 (Repeal of Other Decrees)
The Enforcement Decree of the Korea Overseas Development Corporation Act is hereby repealed.

Article 3 (Amendments to Other Statutes)
① The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Contributions in Kind of State Property is partially amended as follows:
Subparagraph 37 of Article 2 is deleted.

② The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Support for Workers' Housing Stability and Lump-Sum Savings is partially amended as follows:
In Article 2(1) 4, "the President of the Korea Overseas Development Corporation" is replaced with "the President of the Korea International Cooperation Agency".

③ The Regulations on Service of Public Officials Abroad are partially amended as follows:
In Article 24(1), "the Korea Overseas Development Corporation and the Korea Tourism Corporation" is replaced with "the Korea Tourism Corporation and the Korea International Cooperation Agency".

④ The Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on the Management of Government-Invested Institutions is partially amended as follows:
Subparagraph 21 of the attached Table is deleted.

⑤ The Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Economic Crimes is partially amended as follows:
Subparagraph 16 of attached Table 1 is deleted, and subparagraph 61 is newly inserted into attached Table 3 as follows:
61. Korea International Cooperation Agency.

⑥ The Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Aggravated Punishment, etc. of Specific Crimes is partially amended as follows:
Subparagraph 26 of Article 2 is replaced with the following:
26. Korea International Cooperation Agency.

Article 4 (Transitional Measures concerning Budget Requests for Contributions)
Notwithstanding Article 7(2), a budget request for contributions for the year following the establishment of the Agency shall be submitted to the Minister of Foreign Affairs within 30 days after the date of establishment of the Agency.

Article 5 (Notification of Results of Performance of Duties)
Until the Minister of Construction transfers duties concerning free construction technical services to the Agency under the proviso to Article 6(1) of the Addenda to the Act, the Minister shall notify the Agency of the results of the performance of those duties for each half-year by the 15th day of the month following that half-year.
